findings.title: Every success criterion traces to a task; no gaps or scope creep
findings.description: Functional Req coverage: PASS/exit-0 on real designs → Task 4 + Task 4T + Task 5; FAIL + `missing:` lines → Task 4/4T; doctype failure → Task 3/3T/4T; multi-file ordering/exit-1 → Task 3/3T/4T; the five exit-2 triggers with empty stdout → Task 3 (preflight), Task 4 (empty list), Task 3T/4T; `--json` contract → Task 4/4T; worktree-aware template → Task 4/4T. Technical Req coverage: normalization/matching unit tests → Task 2T; real-template file test → Task 3T; real-design command test → Task 4T; build/lint/full-suite + ~300-line cap → Task 6. Integration Req (guide can drop the script) → Task 5 parity sweep. I found no task that fails to trace to a criterion (Task 0 is standard branch setup; Task 1/6 trace to the design's architecture and Implementation Notes step 5). No load-test/NFR requirement exists in the slice, so no `tests/load/` task or CI-gating task is expected.

findings.title: Commit markers use checkbox lines rather than plain lines
findings.description: Tasks 2C/3C/4C/5C/6C are written as `- [ ] **Task 2C: Commit**` (checkbox form) rather than plain `**Commit**:` lines. This conflicts with the "plain lines, never checkboxes" review guidance, but it matches the project's own `AGENTS.md` ("Use checklist format for all task files. Each item and subitem should have a `[ ]` checkbox") and the dominant in-repo pattern (e.g. `931-tasks...md`, `934-tasks...md`, `932-tasks...md` all use `- [x] **Task NC: Commit**`). No action needed unless the house style is being changed; I flag it only because the two conventions disagree.

findings.title: Doctype failure message text lives only in the design, not in a task
findings.description: Task 3 defines `DesignValidationResult` with `reason: 'doctype'` and empty `missing` but no message field, so the exact human string (`frontmatter must declare 'docType: slice-design' (see file-naming-conventions.md)`) must be reproduced by Task 4 from the design's API Contracts. Task 4 says "the frontmatter message for `reason: 'doctype'`", which defers to the design, so the requirement is met — but a junior implementer may not notice the wording lives only in the slice design. Consider naming the constant in Task 3 or Task 4 for one-place definition, consistent with the project rule against scattering comparison values.

findings.title: Task 5 may fix real bugs but commits under a docs: prefix
findings.description: Task 5's parity sweep instructs "Any other difference is a bug: fix it and add a test in the matching test task's file", yet its commit marker (Task 5C) is `docs: record slice 214 parity sweep results`. If the sweep uncovers a genuine mismatch, the resulting change to Tasks 2–4 source (not just docs) warrants a `fix:` commit per the project's semantic-commit rules. This is minor and conditional, but the commit type should match what actually changed.

findings.title: "Unreadable file" exit-2 path is implemented but not tested
findings.description: The design's Functional Requirements name "unreadable" as an exit-2 trigger. Task 3's preflight checks exists/regular/readable, and Task 3T covers the missing-file and directory cases, but no test exercises an existing-but-unreadable file (the "readable" branch specifically). The design's Technical Requirements don't demand that test, and permission-based cases are awkward to exercise portably, so this is informational — but it is the one enumerated exit-2 trigger with no coverage.
